newsitem.title: FRANCE: Oil firms see petrol threat if French strike lasts.
newsitem.headline: Oil firms see petrol threat if French strike lasts.

text.p: Oil companies warned on Friday of fuel shortages in parts of France from next week if a five-day-old truck strike drags through the weekend.
Truckers stepped up a blockade of fuel depots and major provincial arteries on Friday after talks broke down with haulage bosses over pay, driving hours and retirment age.
"The situation has become a bit tougher today. A few new depots have been blocked but we don't have a number," a spokeswoman for oil industry association UFIP said.
Oil companies said Bordeaux in southwestern France was one of the worst areas affected. Parts of the Mediterranean coast and northern France also reported disruption.
A spokesman for Esso France, the French subsidiary of oil giant Exxon, said deliveries to fuel depots had been sealed off in Bordeaux and the Normandy town of Caen.
He said suppliers were managing to bring in supplies from other locations but the main problem was one of time.
"We can handle the logistics now but if this goes through the weekend we could see stations lacking petrol from Monday."
For the time being there was no question of refinery production being reduced, he said.
Truckers have singled out Bordeaux, whose mayor is Prime Minister Alain Juppe, as the main focus of protests, causing huge traffic jams on all access roads.
Airlines at Bordeaux airport said air freight was badly hit.
Paris has so far been spared any major disruption.
Oil company officials said there had been little or no evidence of panic queuing at the pumps for petrol.
But the proportion of people filling up with a full tank, rather than buying a few litres, had risen at big supermarkets.
"People are filling up and the petrol goes quickly," said one supplier. Supermarkets sell about half the petrol in France.
Some petrol stations were already reported to have closed in the Bordeaux area before the weekend started.
